text: {"frames":["The forgotten clock in the attic of the Tower started ticking backwards again, and Olive the keeper of lost things climbed the wet rope to see why. Below her the great mill wheel had stopped, and the hall under it lay silent with its flour sacks stacked to the rafters. Olive pressed her palm to the cold beam and felt the threads humming under the wood. She needed to know how much floor the mill hall covered before the clock ran back to the year she was born. Roughly how many square metres is the mill hall?","Three slow knocks came up through the canal water, and Briony the old lock keeper put down her cheese knife. The sluice gate in the Tower's cellar had sprung a leak, and the water was rising toward the herring barrels. She pulled on her boots, dragged out her measuring cord, and walked the length and width of the hall while the drips counted her steps. The gate could only be sealed if she knew the floor's whole area first. About how many square metres does the mill hall measure?","Wiebke the skate seller ran out onto the canal ice before the sun was up, and the footprints ran out ahead of her. They were small, bare and wet, and they circled a windmill in the middle of the ice, where no windmill had stood yesterday. She followed them with a lantern, her breath smoking, until she stood in the open doorway of a hall with a tin roof and a floor of pale boards. Her quarrel with the miller's son was waiting on the other side of it, and she meant to win it on the measuring. Roughly how many square metres is the hall, from the threshold to the far wall?","\"Mind the watchman,\" whispered Teun, the traveller with no shadow, \"he never speaks, but he sees everything on the dyke.\" They had crept into the Tower's ground floor, where a windmill hall stood open to the fog, and Teun's own shadow had been stolen somewhere on the stairs. He wanted to pay the watchman back for a wrong done to a cheese maker, and the only way was to mark out the hall with white chalk. Each chalk line had to fit the floor exactly, or the watchman would wake. Roughly how many square metres does the mill hall cover?","\"Count with me, quietly,\" said Flora, the talking stork, and the fog repeated her numbers from somewhere above the rafters. The voice was counting steps across the Tower's mill hall, and it had not reached the end yet. Flora had been sent to fetch the answer before the windmill turned for the last time that night, so she stretched her long legs and paced the boards. Her wings twitched every time the voice came too close to her beak. Roughly how many square metres does the mill hall cover?"]}
